doc.title: Pierre Boussaguet interviewed by Matthieu Jaffre, Aix en Provence, France, July 28, 2020

title: Bass as singing counterpoint in Basie's band
summary: He argues Basie's bass line is a counterpoint voice, unlike the groove-only role today.

story.theme_name: Playing with Count Basie: joining, leading, leaving
story.community_name: Playing with Count Basie: the band, its feel and its people

blocks.x: So that’s why in my book I wanted to really, trying to find answers about — what I miss also with that, I grew up with all these, Count Basie records. And especially I wrote about that. When you listen to any bassist playing with the orchestra, in Basie’s band the bass line is not the bass line. It’s like a counterpoint voice, which still has the function of a bass line. The bass is singing. And as a caricature today we put the bass just as a groove. So you spend the whole tune just playing [scats], which is great, but, and then you let all the other instruments play harmony. With Basie, you didn’t have that.

That’s true. Well, Pierre, we are unfortunately coming to the end of our program. I could have gone asking so many more questions. I have one last question. Last but not least. If you were to take a jazz record on a desert island, what record would it be?
